9.5.5. qnav.gravity.map

9.5.5.1. map.py

summary:

Module provides template implementation for gravity correction maps. Due to their high resolution and spatial complexity, methods from the original gravity model base class have had to be adjusted. The largest feature provided by this module is the method for correctly approximating the vertical gravity gradient.

authors:
Prof. Jason Ralph - jfralph@liverpool.ac.uk
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of this module.

class qnav.gravity.map.CircularGrid(num_rings: int = 100, num_angles: int = 50, max_radius: float = 0.25, l_threshold: float = 1.0)[source]

Definition for a circular reference grid from a centre position. Circular grid points used for involving the surrounding data for accurately computing the vertical gravity gradient.

generate_grid(lat: float, lon: float, alt: float) → dict[str, ndarray][source]

Generates a circular grid of query positions surrounding a point. On succession, a dictionary containing the positional and angular information of points surrounding a position of interest are returned. This also includes commonly calculated values step size values.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude position of the point (in decimal degrees).

  • lon (float) – The longitude position of the point (in decimal degrees).

  • alt (float) – The altitude position of the point (in metres).

Returns:

A dictionary holding the calculated positions (lla), NED offsets (ned), azimuth angles (alpha), distances from centre

(psi) and step sizes (delta_psi and delta_alpha).

Return type:

dict[str, np.ndarray]

qnav.gravity.map.set_default_grid(num_rings: int, num_angles: int, max_radius: float, l_threshold: float)[source]

Overwrites the settings to use for the default circular reference grid. This is the grid that will be used by default for calculating the vertical gravity gradient.

Parameters:

  • num_rings (int) – Number of radial distance steps.

  • num_angles (int) – Number of azimuth angle steps.

  • max_radius (float) – Maximum radial distance (in degrees).

  • l_threshold (float) – Threshold for internal points (in metres).

class qnav.gravity.map.GravityMap(base_model: GravityModel, geoid_model: GeoidModel | None, map_dir: Path | None, auto_download: bool = True)[source]

An extension to the abstract base class GravityModel that provides re-worked methods for handling high-resolution lookup maps.

abstract get_anomaly(lat: float, lon: float) → float[source]

Calculates the gravity anomaly for given position. Retrieves the gravity anomaly value for the requested position (in m/s^2) at the base surface. For gravity maps this value is interpolated from its dataset, following possible conversion.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

Returns:

The gravity anomaly value (in m/s^2).

Return type:

float

Calculates the gravity disturbance for given position. Retrieves the gravity disturbance value for the requested position (in m/s^2) at the base surface. For gravity maps this value is interpolated from its dataset, following possible conversion.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

Returns:

The gravity disturbance value (in m/s^2).

Return type:

float

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

Returns:

float

Calculates the gravity disturbance for multiple given positions. Retrieves the gravity disturbance value for the requested position (in m/s^2) at the base surface. For gravity maps this value is interpolated from its dataset, following possible conversion.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

calc_gravity_xyz(lat: float, lon: float, alt: float) → ndarray[source]

Calculates and returns the gravitational acceleration vector. Computes the gravity acceleration X/North, Y/East and Z/Down components (in m/s^2) for the given location and altitude offset.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (float) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

Returns:

The local gravity vector for the XYZ components (in m/s^2).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray (3-elements)

calc_gravity_xyz_vec(lat: ndarray, lon: ndarray, alt: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

In a vectorised batch, calculates and returns the gravitational acceleration for the X/North, Y/East and Z/Down axes (in m/s^2) for the given location and altitude offset. Ideal when calculating gravity for a large number of positions.

Parameters:

  • lat (np.array) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (np.array) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (np.array) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

Returns:

The local gravity vector for the XYZ components (in m/s^2).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray (N-by-3 elements)

calc_vertical_grad(lat: float, lon: float, alt: float, step: float = 100, circular_grid: CircularGrid = None) → float[source]

Calculates the vertical gradient of gravity. Computes the vertical change in gravity (∂g/∂r) of the Z/Down component (in m/s^2). This is primary used for gravity map-matching related calculations.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (float) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

  • step (float) – The step size (in metres) for calculating the gradient. To be used when the gradient cannot be computed directly.

Returns:

The vertical gravity gradient (in m/s^2).

Return type:

float

calc_vertical_grad_vec(lat: ndarray, lon: ndarray, alt: ndarray, step: float = 100, circular_grid: CircularGrid = None) → ndarray[source]

In a vectorised batch, calculates the vertical gradient of gravity. Computes the vertical change in gravity (∂g/∂r) of the Z/Down component (in m/s^2). This is primary used for gravity map-matching related calculations.

Parameters:

  • lat (np.ndarray) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (np.ndarray) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (np.ndarray) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

  • step (float) – The step size (in metres) for calculating the gradient. To be used when the gradient cannot be computed directly.

Returns:

The vertical gravity gradient (in m/s^2).

Return type:

float
